name: TVBench
intro: TVBench是一个新颖的开源视频多项选择问答基准，旨在评估视频语言模型中的时间理解能力。它通过设计具有时间挑战性的候选答案、减少文本偏见以及排除需要先验知识的问题来解决现有视频语言基准的局限性。TVBench要求模型高度依赖时间理解，而非静态信息或世界知识。
org: University of Santiago de Compostela, University of Amsterdam, University of Technology Nuremberg
build_method: 八个公开视频源、10类时间任务、任务专用模板、时间困难干扰项、答案平衡与文本/单帧/乱序偏差筛查
eval_feature: 纯时间多选问答, 平衡候选, 单帧/乱序/倒放诊断
scale: 2654组视频多选问答，覆盖10类时间任务
build_method_en: Eight public video sources, ten temporal tasks, task-specific templates, temporally hard distractors, answer balancing, and text-only/single-frame/shuffle bias checks
eval_feature_en: Temporal-only MCQA, balanced candidates, single-frame/shuffle/reverse diagnostics
intro_en: TVBench is a novel open-source video multiple-choice question answering benchmark designed to evaluate temporal understanding in video language models. It addresses limitations of existing video language benchmarks by creating temporally challenging candidate answers, reducing textual biases, and excluding questions requiring prior knowledge. TVBench demands models rely heavily on temporal understanding rather than static information or world knowledge.
scale_en: 2,654 video MCQA pairs across ten temporal tasks

drawio_review_note: Aligned with TVBench arXiv:2410.07752v3 Sections 4-5 and official daniel-cores/tvbench repository and FunAILab/TVBench dataset card. TVBench is designed around three anti-shortcut requirements: a random single frame must be insufficient, question and answer text must not reveal the answer, and world knowledge must not solve the item. The authors define ten tasks: Action Count; Object Shuffle, Object Count, and Moving Direction; Action Localization and Unexpected Action; Action Sequence, Scene Transition, and Egocentric Sequence; plus temporally opposed Action Antonyms. Videos and annotations are adapted from Perception Test, CLEVRER, STAR, MoVQA, Charades-STA, NTU RGB+D, FunQA, and CSV. Task-specific templates avoid LLM wording artifacts. Distractors are temporally plausible alternatives, correct-option frequencies are balanced for applicable tasks, and world-knowledge questions are excluded. The latest paper release contains 2,654 video multiple-choice QA pairs. Evaluation uses exact choice accuracy by task and overall. Text-only and random-frame models should remain near chance; shuffled and reversed video tests verify that success depends on temporal order rather than static appearance or answer priors.
